title: Synora API — operations
description: Every number here is counted by the API process itself, next to the code that did the work. See app/core/metrics.py.

panels.title: Requests per second, by route
panels.description: Route templates, never paths: `/tts/batch/{job_id}` is one series.

panels.title: Latency to the status line (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Stops at the status line. On `/tts/speech` the audio comes after it, so this is time-to-headers there and the relay is its own panel below.

panels.title: Refusals per minute, by code
panels.description: The stable `code` from the error body, not the status. `402 insufficient_balance` is a customer who needs a top-up; `503 tts_key_rejected` is our own credential — both are refusals and only one is anybody's emergency.

panels.title: 5xx share (5m)
panels.description: Zero is zero here, not "No data": the 5xx series does not exist until the first one happens, and an error-rate panel that cannot tell "nothing broke" from "nothing scraped" is worse than no panel.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Syntheses in flight that never falls back to zero is a leaked gauge — or a leaked hold.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: From prometheus_client's process collector, which needs /proc: empty on macOS, present in production. Resets on every deploy — a counter that drops to zero at the same moment is not a bug.

panels.title: Syntheses per minute, by outcome
panels.description: `billed` moved audio and charged for it, `free` never got a byte out of upstream and charged nothing, `replay` re-synthesised for a retry under a spent idempotency key and charged nothing either.

panels.title: Time to first audio, from upstream (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Headers are the GPU queueing up; the relay includes the audio, so it grows with the text. Alert on the first, read the second.

panels.title: Characters billed per minute
panels.description: The one quantity the price book prices. Replays are excluded — they charge nothing.

panels.title: Upstream failures per minute, by code
panels.description: `tts_key_rejected` and `tts_quota_exhausted` are ours to fix and are logged at ERROR; `tts_unreachable` is the tunnel; `tts_rejected_input` is the caller's own text and is not an incident.

panels.title: Audio relayed
panels.description: Bandwidth, counted for replays too — those bytes are real.

panels.title: Credits per minute
panels.description: Micros on the wire, credits on the axis. Counted after the commit, so a rolled-back settlement never appears here.

panels.title: Held right now
panels.description: Credit committed to sessions that have not settled. It should spike during calls and fall back; a floor that climbs across a quiet night is a hold that never came back, and `POST /admin/reconcile` is what recovers it.

panels.title: Ledger divergence
panels.description: Wallets whose balance disagreed with their own ledger on the last reconciliation pass. The only number here that should be alerted on at any value above zero — and it only refreshes when a pass runs.

panels.title: Credit in wallets
panels.description: What customers are holding, by bucket. Bonus is spent first because it expires.

panels.title: Open sessions, by status
panels.description: Read from the rows at scrape time. `pending` that never leaves is a ticket nobody claimed.

panels.title: Open batch jobs, by state
panels.description: `queued` means upstream has never seen it. With no broker a job only moves when somebody reads it, so a pile here on a dev box is normal and a pile in production is a dead worker.

panels.title: Settlements and reaps per minute
panels.description: A reap is a hold that came back late. Steady reaping means something is dying mid-stream. `clamped` is a settlement that priced above the session's ceiling: it is billed at the ceiling and the row is flagged `disputed`, so any value here is somebody's bug rather than a busy day.

panels.title: Process
panels.description: From prometheus_client's own collector. Absent on macOS, which has no /proc.

panels.title: Batch jobs finished per hour, by state
panels.description: `expired` is a job we stopped polling and settled at the last usage upstream admitted to; `cancelled` is a user who changed their mind. Both leave the hold released — that is the invariant, and this is where you notice it is not.

panels.title: Reconciliation activity per hour
panels.description: Nothing runs this on a timer yet — `POST /admin/reconcile` is the only caller — so a flat zero here means nobody has looked, not that there was nothing to find. `synora_reconcile_diverged` above only refreshes when a pass runs, for the same reason.

panels.title: Audio transcribed per minute
panels.description: Seconds of audio charged for, as the transcription service counted them — never as we estimated them. The hold is the estimate; this is the bill.

panels.title: Transcription latency (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Upload plus inference, from our side of the socket. A cold model load lands in here too, which is what `stt_not_ready` is about.

panels.title: Transcription failures per minute, by code
panels.description: `stt_key_rejected` is our own token and is logged at ERROR; `stt_not_ready` is a model still loading and clears itself; `stt_rejected_input` is the caller's own audio and is not an incident.

panels.title: Live sessions in flight
panels.description: Each one holds a GPU slot upstream for its whole duration — the service's own documentation says a live session occupies the card. A number that never returns to zero is a leaked session, which is also a leaked hold.

panels.title: Live sessions per hour, by how they ended
panels.description: `stop_requested` is a client saying goodbye. `heartbeat_timeout` is a tab somebody abandoned, `grace_exhausted` is the cap, and a rise in `client_disconnected` is a network worth looking at.

panels.title: Speech against connection time
panels.description: The gap between the two lines is the silence VAD trimmed — billed through the connection fee rather than as audio. Sockets far above audio means people are holding lines open without speaking.
